findings.evidence: `LaplacianMaximumPrinciple.lean:46-49` uses `ContinuousOn` only to call `hK.exists_isMaxOn`; Mathlib has `UpperSemicontinuousOn.exists_isMaxOn` at `Mathlib/Topology/Semicontinuity/Basic.lean:744-748` and `ContinuousOn.upperSemicontinuousOn` at lines `835-836`.
findings.fix: Replace `hcont : ContinuousOn f K` by `husc : UpperSemicontinuousOn f K` in the helper and public max theorem, use `husc.exists_isMaxOn hne hK`, and derive the continuous corollary if needed via `ContinuousOn.upperSemicontinuousOn`.
findings.issue: The maximum theorem assumes `hcont : ContinuousOn f K`, but the proof only needs existence of a compact maximum; Mathlib’s natural API is `UpperSemicontinuousOn.exists_isMaxOn`.

findings.evidence: `LaplacianMaximumPrinciple.lean:60-63` uses `ContinuousOn` only to call `hK.exists_isMinOn`; Mathlib has `LowerSemicontinuousOn.exists_isMinOn` at `Mathlib/Topology/Semicontinuity/Basic.lean:76-79` and `ContinuousOn.lowerSemicontinuousOn` at lines `255-256`.
findings.fix: Replace `hcont : ContinuousOn f K` by `hlsc : LowerSemicontinuousOn f K` in the helper and public min theorem, use `hlsc.exists_isMinOn hne hK`, and keep a continuous corollary only as a specialization if desired.
findings.issue: The minimum theorem similarly assumes `hcont : ContinuousOn f K`, but compact minimum existence only needs lower semicontinuity.

summary: The boundary handoff is stated with stronger regularity on K than the Mathlib extrema APIs require. Generalize the max/min hypotheses to the one-sided semicontinuity actually used for existence of the relevant extremum.
